newsitem.title: GERMANY: Masked gunman holds employee in German bank.
newsitem.headline: Masked gunman holds employee in German bank.

text.p: An armed man took a hostage in a Munich bank on Thursday and police said they were ready to hand over ransom money and a getaway car.

A police spokesman said money had been brought to the scene but was not yet in the hostage-taker's hands. Officers had been able to talk to the hostage, a 24-year-old male bank employee, and establish he had not been injured.

"We will meet his demands as far as possible with the aim of saving the hostage's life," the spokesman said. He declined to gave any details of the demands. Asked if the man had set an ultimatum, he said "certain deadlines" had been agreed.

The masked man entered the bank in the southern city's Grosshadern district at around 8.30 a.m (0730 GMT). Two other people in the bank were able to flee. It was not clear if the man originally intended to rob the bank.
Police said they were not sure if the man was acting alone and if he was also holding other hostages. They described him as aggressive and potentially violent.
Police sealed off the area shortly after the incident began. It came almost exactly a year after Munich police had to deal with two hostage dramas within 24 hours.
They first stormed a bank where an armed man was holding three people hostage for a ransom of four million marks ($2.8 million). All the captives and the hostage-taker were unharmed.
Hours later they shot dead a man who threatened to kill his girlfriend and a policeman. The man fired at police after they came to investigate a domestic row.
He then grabbed an officer who tried to stop him fleeing and held him captive for half an hour.
Police also shot dead a man who held 12 people in a dental surgery in the nearby town of Dachau in February.
